findings.title: Test doesn't exercise the queue-drain path in stream_close()
findings.claim: When stream_close() runs in this test, the eof entry has already finished, so queue_drained is ready and only the gate at rpc.cc:293 is exercised; dropping the drain at rpc.cc:557-570 would still pass even though a hook frame queued just before the mark can reach it.

findings.title: Base-case test failure mode depends on scheduling, may abort instead of throwing as…
findings.claim: The try/catch accepts the hook succeeding, and the 10 yield() calls don't force the batch-flush poller despite the comment, so outside debug builds base can abort in ~output_stream instead of failing with the BOOST message the commit claims; BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(stream_send_empty_frame().get(), rpc::closed_error) would fail on base every time.

findings.title: Claim that window is 'held open deterministically' is overstated
findings.claim: The server keeps draining while close() is parked, so the client's _error could be set first; base would then refuse via _error and pass, though this is unlikely in practice.

findings.title: Docs wrongly say reading a source until it throws is sufficient to close it
findings.claim: The docs say reading until it 'throws' closes a source, but an unmarshall failure in process_one_buffer never calls close_source(), so an application that follows the docs and stops there never triggers stream_close().

findings.title: Docs wrongly claim connection shuts down only once both halves are closed
findings.claim: Peer eof, loop errors, and abort_all_streams() all stop the connection without both halves being closed, contradicting the commit's claim of 'never shut down' otherwise.

findings.title: Comment wrongly says path is only exceptional if an entry failed
findings.claim: The comment states the path is '(exceptional if an entry failed)', but a failed send_entry calls abort() and then done.set_value(), not an exception.

findings.title: Comment wrongly claims nothing else waits on _outgoing_queue_ready
findings.claim: stop_send_loop() still waits on _outgoing_queue_ready in when_all (rpc.cc:225); it just now gets the ready placeholder.

findings.title: Comment overclaims that _error is only set by the stop() that follows
findings.claim: abort() and loop errors can also set _error during the new drain wait, contradicting the comment's claim that only the following stop() sets it.

findings.title: New put(std::span) test override lacks API-level guard, breaks build at API levels 7/8
findings.claim: The put(std::span) override has no #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 guard, unlike loopback_socket.hh:144, so rpc_test stops compiling at API levels 7/8, which CMakeLists.txt still allows.

findings.title: close_entered_cv.wait has no timeout, regression could hang until 300s harness timeout
findings.claim: A regression that never reaches close() hangs until the 300 second harness timeout because close_entered_cv.wait has no timeout of its own.

findings.title: Early test assertion failure leaves sink unclosed, aborting the process instead of…
findings.claim: A failing BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(hooks.size(), 2u) (or any earlier throw) drops the unclosed sink, and ~sink_impl's assert aborts instead of reporting; existing stream tests share this issue, and deferred_close(sink) would avoid it.

findings.title: const_cast used in hook_capturing_compressor_factory::negotiate instead of existing…
findings.claim: The same file uses a mutable member (cfactory, rpc_test.cc:330) for this purpose elsewhere, making the const_cast inconsistent.

findings.title: Backport claim only partly holds for branches lacking put(std::span)
findings.claim: The test's put(std::span) (added 2025-10) won't apply to branches from 2023-10 to 2025-10 which have the bug, though the fix commit itself is self-contained.

findings.title: Commits lack Signed-off-by DCO line required by contributing docs
findings.claim: None of the three commits has a Signed-off-by line, though doc/contributing.md asks for a DCO sign-off (though repo history mostly skips it).

findings.title: Commits and PR contain Claude attribution trailers, violating user's CLAUDE.md policy
findings.claim: All three commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers and the PR body ends with 'Generated with Claude Code', which the global CLAUDE.md forbids.

findings.title: Fixes/Refs issue links may resolve against the wrong repo, risking auto-close of wrong…
findings.claim: Fixes #3663 / Refs #3653 resolve against dkropachev/ironweave, whose links base 5cc62de6 repointed; they likely mean upstream issues but this couldn't be confirmed because the fetch failed, and if so, merging could auto-close the wrong local issue.

findings.title: _stream_closing flag claimed as a hazard
findings.claim: The _stream_closing flag is not a hazard because enqueue_zero_frame only runs from the constructor.

findings.title: Size of test's socket wrappers questioned
findings.claim: The size of the test's socket wrappers is justified.

findings.title: Parent-client connection claimed to have an equivalent race window
findings.claim: The parent-client connection has no equivalent window, because stop_send_loop() sets _error before closing.

findings.title: Audit's claimed use-after-free on st does not happen
findings.claim: The audit's use-after-free on st doesn't happen: the broken shared_promise resolves the parked close.
